paras: The threatened lynching of George Foster occurred near Smithfield, Fulton County, Illinois, in September 1888, when Foster, accused of outraging his nine-year-old daughter, was reported to have narrowly escaped lynching before being held in the county jail at Lewistown. He was not harmed, and no crowd or act against him was described. The case drew notice mainly through a Canton dispatch carried in the Northwest and through the Canton Register's open regret that he had not been lynched.

According to the Canton Register, Foster's daughter was nine years old and "motherless," and arrangements had been made for her to live with the family of the railroad section boss at Seville. The Register charged that on the Tuesday evening of the week before its September 27 issue, while taking the girl from a relative's house to the section boss's, Foster committed a "nameless outrage" on her. Her behavior afterward aroused suspicion, and on a promise of protection she made a statement that the paper said a surgical examination "verified."

By September 24 Foster was in jail at Lewistown, unable to give bond on charges of rape and incest, and one news brief gave the 24th as the day he was jailed. The girl was also reported to have said that he had choked her mother to death and threatened to kill her if she told, a death that had been attributed at the time to heart disease or apoplexy. The Register wrote that "feeling in the Smithtield neighborhood is so intense that he barely escaped lynching," and the Canton special said he "narrowly escaped lynching"; neither said who threatened him or when.

The Register expected that the murder charge might not be sustained and noted that the courts could not hang Foster for the assault unless the girl died, whose condition it called precarious. No report of a trial or sentence was found in the coverage.

The earliest report was a Canton special dated September 24 that the St. Paul Daily Globe printed the next day under the headline "Material for a Hanging," running it on two pages of the same issue. The same text, credited to the Peoria Evening Journal's Canton correspondent, appeared in the Jamestown Weekly Alert in Dakota as "Judge Lynch Delinquent." Minnesota weeklies such as the Worthington Advance and the Kanabec County Times reduced it to a one-line brief on the incest charge with no mention of lynching.

Closer to home, the Canton Register headed its account "A Fiendish Father Who Ought to Have Been Lynched" and said his crime surpassed another recent Fulton County case, the "horrible double crime" charged to "Hud" Farris. Its editor wrote that it "really seems a pity that he did escape it," arguing that the statute law provided no suitable penalty for his alleged crime. No paper gave Foster's race.
Accounts differed on the season of the wife's death: the Register placed it the previous spring and attributed it to heart disease, while the Canton special said last winter and "supposed apoplexy."

reader.title: Threatened lynching of George Foster
bases: Two accounts say Foster, jailed on a charge of outraging his daughter, 'barely' or 'narrowly escaped lynching' (A1, A3); no mob action is described, so this is a threatened lynching.

Foster was not killed; he was held in the county jail at Lewistown (A1, A3). The papers report only that local feeling nearly led to his lynching, over an accusation of rape and incest, without describing any crowd or act (A1, A3).

The local Canton Register (A3) and a Canton special telegraphed to the St. Paul Globe and through Peoria (A1, A4) both say Foster was jailed and narrowly escaped lynching, though both originate in Canton and may share a source.

accounts.label: Canton Register (local)
accounts.gist: Foster committed the outrage while taking his daughter to the section boss's house at Seville; her confession was verified by surgical examination; neighborhood feeling was so intense he barely escaped lynching, and the editor regretted that he did.

accounts.label: Canton special (wire)
accounts.gist: Foster was jailed at Lewiston unable to give bond on charges of rape and incest; the girl said he choked his wife to death last winter and threatened to kill her if she told; he narrowly escaped lynching.

accounts.label: Western news brief
accounts.gist: Foster was placed in jail on the 24th on a charge of incest with his nine-year-old daughter.

framing.detail: The Canton Register's headline said Foster 'Ought to Have Been Lynched' and its editor wrote that it 'really seems a pity that he did escape it'.
The St. Paul Globe headed the Canton special 'Material for a Hanging' and the Jamestown Alert headed it 'Judge Lynch Delinquent'.
The Minnesota news briefs gave only the arrest and charge, without mention of lynching.
